explanation: For each pattern prefix, record which cells can end a matching walk. A cell is reachable for the next value when one of its four neighbors ended the previous prefix. Keep only two layers; revisiting cells is allowed by this question.
timeComplexity: O(R C L) time for an R-by-C grid and length-L pattern. There are at most RCL cell/offset states per memo scope; C++/Java recreate that scope for each starting cell.
spaceComplexity: O(R C) auxiliary space. Layered DP keeps two Boolean grids; suffix search keeps cell/offset memo entries and recursion.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The reachable layer for pattern position i contains exactly the cells that can end a walk matching the prefix through i. A next cell is reachable precisely when it has the next required value and an adjacent cell belonged to the previous layer. Induction proves that any final marked cell yields a complete walk, including walks that revisit cells.
walkthrough: For [[5,8],[9,2]] and pattern [5,8,5,9], use (0,0)→(0,1)→(0,0)→(1,0). The first cell is legally reused, so return true. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: This EPI variant permits cell reuse, unlike Blind75 Word Search.
Moves must be horizontal or vertical; staying in place is not a step.
An empty pattern is matched without consuming a cell.
